body.text: Magnetic Confinement Scaling and the High-Field Revolution

What separates informed decisions about The Physics of Commercial Fusion from costly guesswork in science? Primary context, measurable criteria, and disciplined execution form the foundation of lasting value.

In magnetic confinement fusion, the Lawson criterion dictates which plasma pressure scales with the fourth power of magnetic field strength (B^4). Historically, large tokamaks like ITER required immense building-sized footprints because low-temperature niobium-tin superconductors saturated around 12 Tesla. The advent of Rare-Earth Barium Copper Oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconducting (HTS) tape allows engineers to generate sustained 20-Tesla fields in compact, factory-assembled coils.
Core Plasma & Magnetics Physics

items: REBCO Tape Epitaxy: Thin-film ceramic superconductors deposited onto flexible hastelloy steel ribbons, conducting over 500 amperes per square millimeter at 20 Kelvin.
Tokamak Plasma Volumetric Scaling: Quadrupling magnetic field strength enables a forty-fold reduction in reactor core volume while achieving the exact same fusion power output.
Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) Stability: Suppressing edge-localized modes (ELMs) and neoclassical tearing instabilities through real-time resonant magnetic perturbation coils.
Tritium Breeding Blankets: Using liquid lithium-lead eutectic blankets to capture 14.1 MeV fusion neutrons, breeding tritium fuel while extracting thermal energy for steam turbines.

body.text: Quench Protection and Cryogenic Mechanical Integrity

At 20 Tesla, magnetic Lorentz forces exert structural pressures comparable to the deepest trenches of the ocean. Superconducting coils must be encased in cryogenic stainless-steel casings and monitored with fiber-optic Bragg sensors to detect local thermal runaway (quenches) within milliseconds before magnet self-destruction will occur.
